items.title: Dynamics of random recurrent neural networks: colored noise and sublinear activations
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: German Mato, Facundo Rigatuso, Gonzalo Torroba
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dynamics of recurrent neural networks with random couplings, sublinear odd activation functions, and temporally correlated noise. Using large N methods, we determine stationary correlations and distinguish the loss of local linear stability from the onset of chaos, characterized by a positive largest Lyapunov exponent. These thresholds delimit an intermediate regime in which local instability coexists with asymptotic stability under a common noise history. Their separation depends on both the noise correlation time and the asymptotic growth of the activation function. We show that internal noise with any finite correlation time cuts off the divergence of the network's intrinsic correlation time tau_corr at the edge of chaos; it exhibits a critical scaling tau_{corr,max} propto 1/sqrt{D_0}, where D_0 is the integrated noise strength. Static random input instead produces coincident thresholds and a divergent correlation time. We also calculate the frequency-dependent participation dimension from a four-point correlation function. Its zero-frequency value is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the network correlation time, predicting a smooth minimum at the weak-noise chaos threshold. Numerical simulations support the large-network predictions and reveal appreciable finite-size effects.

items.title: A Formalizable Proof of the No-Supervenience Theorem: A Diagonal Limitation on the Viability of Physicalist Theories of Consciousness
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Cathy M Reason
items.summary: arXiv:2307.10178v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The no-supervenience theorem limits the capacity of physicalist theories to provide a comprehensive account of human consciousness. The proof of the theorem is difficult to formalize because it relies on both alethic and epistemic notions of possibility. This article outlines a formalizable proof using predicate modal logic in which the epistemic inferences are expressed in terms of an existing mathematical formalism, the inference device (Wolpert, 2008). The resulting proof shows definitely that any physicalist theory which describes a self-aware, intelligent system must be internally inconsistent.

items.title: The medium is the message: How neurometabolic entanglement generates conscious experience
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Terrence W. Deacon, Miguel Garcia-Valdecasas, Michael Jacob
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most neuroscientific accounts of consciousness assume that conscious experience is constituted by the information conveyed between neurons. The physical-chemical details of the metabolic and physiological processes that convey this information are correspondingly presumed to be relevant only insofar as they support the organization of information processes. We describe an alternative perspective that denies this presumed independence of the processing of neural information and the metabolic-physiological details of these processes. We call this alternative paradigm the theory of neuro-metabolic entanglement (NME). NME proposes that mental experience exemplifies the inseparability of the organization of neural information processes from the constraints imposed by the material-energetic properties of the neural medium itself. Central to this account is a recursive, M\"obius-like loop of neural connections that entangles patterns of forebrain information processing with midbrain regulatory systems that modulate forebrain metabolism. This enables patterns of neural activity to indirectly modify the global distribution of metabolic resources underlying these information processes. It also constitutes a bottleneck that integrates diverse neural processes into an adaptively relevant unitary experience organized in terms of the global redistribution of metabolic support. Computational models of neural function cannot treat energy supply as a fixed background parameter; our proposed M\"obius-like loop of neuro-metabolic entanglement offers a framework for future models in which neural activity is dynamically and recursively modulated by the network's own metabolism. Recognizing this entanglement is a first step toward dissolving the explanatory gap highlighted by the so-called "hard problem" of consciousness.

items.title: Gate-Based Feature Importance in Simulation-Based Inference for EEG: A Cautionary Tale
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Shrivatsa Deshmukh, Sasha Brenner, Thomas R. Kn\"osche, Nico Scherf
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulation-based inference (SBI) provides a powerful way to fit mechanistic models to data, but offers little insight into which information in the data shapes the inferred parameter values. It could therefore benefit from robust and inexpensive interpretability methods. Learned weighting mechanisms such as feature gates provide a potential route to low-cost interpretability, although their interpretation assumes that predictive training reveals which inputs drive performance. We examined this assumption in a computational neuroscience setting, where neural posterior estimation (NPE) is used to infer four physiological parameters of a dynamical model of interacting neuronal populations (Jansen-Rit). We tested whether the learned gate weights captured feature importance by comparing them with a retrain-based ablation benchmark, in which each feature was removed in turn and the NPE retrained. We considered two jointly trained gates: independent sigmoid weights and competing softmax weights. If these reliably reflect feature importance, they should align with the ablation-based estimates. Across nine independent training seeds, however, gate-based and ablation-based importance were negatively correlated (Spearman's rho approximately -0.61 for sigmoid gating and -0.56 for softmax gating). The feature that ablation identified as most important, total signal power, was among the features the gate down-weighted most, despite gating costing negligible predictive accuracy. These results extend a pattern previously documented for attention mechanisms in natural language processing and for explainability methods in electroencephalography (EEG) deep learning to the simulation-based inference setting, and suggest caution when interpreting learned gate weights as measures of causal feature importance in scientific machine-learning pipelines.

items.title: Music Between Two Minds: Individual Signatures, Shared States, and the Emergence of Creative Interaction
items.subtitle: ARXIV · Q-BIO.NC · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Tatsuya Daikoku, Risa Kobayashi, Rina Tabuchi, Yoshia Abe, Yasuo Kuniyoshi
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Some of the most valued forms of human creativity arise between people-in conversation, collaboration, and improvised music-yet how two minds jointly regulate the flow of novelty in real time remains unknown. Here we examined the information dynamics of interpersonal improvisation using 986 professional jazz improvisations. Pitch-based fluctuations of uncertainty and surprise behaved as signatures of individual identity: the two partners differed within 90% of takes, performers were identifiable from single solos and the separation between partners persisted undiminished across turns and takes. Rhythm-based fluctuations showed the reverse organization: partners were statistically indistinguishable within a take yet shifted together from take to take, and this shared state drifted gradually as each performance progressed, with each performer moving away from their own past at the same rate as from their partner's. Beyond joint drift, solo hand-offs revealed turn-by-turn complementarity: when one performer exceeded their own average surprise in the predictive dynamics of improvisation, the partner's next solo fell below their own, in both pitch and rhythm and in all duos. Improvising pairs thus neither fuse into one system nor remain two independent ones: they preserve individual melodic voices while sharing a rhythmic state, within which moment-to-moment push-pull continually rebalances their interaction. Individuality and togetherness thus coexist, carried by different musical dimensions, a measurable organization of creativity that emerges between minds.

items.title: The Impact of Markovian Errors on Random Circuits
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Anthony M. Polloreno, Timothy Proctor, Robin Blume-Kohout
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Randomized benchmarking (RB) returns a single decay parameter or gate error rate, but when the noise is gate-dependent that parameter is notoriously difficult to interpret. We study RB and related random-circuit benchmarks under small gate-local Markovian noise by factorizing each noisy gate into its ideal action followed by the exponential of a small error generator and then perturbing the RB $\mathscr{L}$ matrix, which models the RB decay. For any low-error gate set that satisfies the requirements of RB (it is a sequence-asymptotic unitary 2-design), we show that Pauli-stochastic error rates contribute linearly to the RB decay parameter, while Hamiltonian error rates contribute through a gauge-invariant quadratic form. Pauli-correlation and active generators are absent from the linear term and enter only at higher order. For the single-qubit native gate set $\{X_{\pi/2},Y_{\pi/2}\}$ we derive this quadratic form explicitly in terms of three first-order gauge-invariant (FOGI) coordinates: the two intrinsic over-rotations and one relational axis-tilt error. The resulting formula explains the dependence of DRB on the sampling distribution and the compilation dependence of CRB. These results turn RB decay rates into interpretable functions of experimentally meaningful elementary error rates.

items.title: Rank-One Loss Maximizes the Spectral Response Strength of Passive Full-Order Exceptional Points
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Jan Wiersig
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider finite-dimensional non-Hermitian systems in which all modes coalesce at a single exceptional point. For a rank-one anti-Hermitian contribution, the spectral response strength is computed exactly. For passive systems, we then derive a sharp upper bound at fixed exceptional-point decay rate and show that it is reached only when the decay operator has rank one, corresponding to a single independent dissipative direction. This establishes rank-one loss as the optimal configuration for enhancing the response of a full-order exceptional point. The bound holds for arbitrary order and improves on earlier passive estimates beyond second order. Two third-order trimers illustrate the result: a rank-one-loss system saturates the bound, whereas a passive rank-two-loss realization remains below it. The result turns dissipation into a design resource: concentrating the loss into a single effective dissipative direction maximizes the highest-order spectral response of a passive full-order exceptional-point device.

items.title: High-fidelity entanglement of two spectrally-distinct solid state emitters
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Daniel R. E. Hodgson, Pieter Kok
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solid state quantum emitters with electronic spin properties can be entangled using optical interferometric which-path erasure techniques that rely on identical frequencies and linewidths of the emitters. This promises a powerful, fast and scalable platform for quantum technologies. Using current protocols, a pair of emitters embedded in a waveguide interferometer can be deterministically prepared in a maximally entangled state. However, the amount of entanglement diminishes rapidly with increasing separation of the emission lines and variations in the linewidths of the emitters. Solid state emitters such as quantum dots are subject to intrinsic variations in the fabrication process. Therefore, manufacturing the required number of identical emitters on a chip is not scalable. In this Letter, we present a method that uses readily available pairs of entangled photons to entangle solid state emitters with large transition frequency separations and linewidth variations, circumventing the need to fabricate optically identical emitters. We demonstrate a concurrence of C = 0.95 for typical quantum dots using narrowband photon inputs.

items.title: Quantum Fokker-Planck solvers as trainable generative models
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Tariq Mahassen, Marcin Jastrzebski, Oleksandr Kyriienko
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze generative models based on quantum solvers of stochastic differential equations. Unlike the common approach based on layered variational quantum circuits with parameterized rotations, we parameterize the potential of a Langevin process. The associated Fokker-Planck (FP) equations are Hermitianized and solved using a linear combination of cosine operators implemented through quantum singular value transformation. By encoding the square root of the stationary density, the model enables sampling through computational-basis measurements and is efficiently controlled by coefficients of the block-encoded diagonal potential. We train the proposed model to match empirical distributions within the family described by FP equations, demonstrating parameter recovery for multivariate probability distributions. Crucially, the model remains trainable at scale. Sample-efficient and convex optimization for in-distribution targets arises from a physics-informed inductive bias and holds regardless of the dimensionality of the problem. We provide circuit constructions and efficient block encodings of the main components of the algorithm and analyze resource requirements. Our approach frames quantum generative learning as quantum model discovery and provides a foundation for extending this framework to high-dimensional, strongly correlated scientific data.

items.title: Automating quantum circuit optimization with AI agents
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Marcos Crichigno, Steve Flammia
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compiling quantum algorithms for real devices involves hard optimization problems that can decide whether an algorithm runs at scale. We present a general method for solving such problems with AI agents, with every result certified. It builds on autoresearch loops, in which agents iteratively improve programs against a fixed evaluator and which have recently improved quantum cryptanalysis circuits, and adds two elements: a frozen, exact verifier certifies every result, and this verifier, together with the challenge around it, is built by an agent that formulates the problem with a researcher and validates the verifier against a solved case, deliberately broken solutions and published results before any solution exists. The method applies to any optimization problem whose solutions can be verified exactly and efficiently. We apply it to three compilation problems in quantum simulation, namely fermion-to-qubit encoding, Hamiltonian layout and unitary synthesis. In each, the agents improved substantially on published or standard constructions, reducing the cost being optimized by up to 73% at the largest sizes tested and outperforming a state-of-the-art optimizer for fermion-to-qubit encodings. Every submission is a program accompanied by its agent's notes, so the ideas behind each improvement are recorded in human-readable form; later agents built on them, and we describe them here. These results open the way to automated, certified discovery across quantum circuit design and beyond.

items.title: Finite Systems in the Space of Projective Measurements
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Miguel Flores R., Carlos A. Mu\~noz
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the dynamics of two-level systems using the quasidistribution $Q$ function projected onto the space of collective measurements. Particular attention is given to evolution under Hamiltonians that are invariant under particle permutations, for pure states that are either invariant or noninvariant under such permutations. This requires constructing an approximate analog of the star product between quasidistribution functions: the projected $Q$ function of a product of two operators is expressed approximately in terms of the individual operators' $Q$ and $P$ functions. We rewrite the Liouville equation to determine approximate state dynamics and compare the result with exact evolution using the Hellinger distance. Overall, the method performs well for permutation-invariant pure states and Hamiltonians, whereas deviations arise for arbitrary pure states and noninvariant Hamiltonians.

items.title: Qubits Are Not Enough: Deflation and Measurement Limits in Variational Quantum Modal Analysis
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Bikalpa Gautam, Akil Raj Subedi
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Amplitude encoding stores an N-degree-of-freedom structural mode using ceiling(log2 N) qubits. This article develops an evaluation framework for variational quantum eigensolvers in finite-element structural dynamics. A Cholesky transformation maps the generalized eigenproblem to a symmetric mass-orthonormal Hamiltonian, ensuring Euclidean quantum-state orthogonality equals structural mass orthogonality. For higher modes, the deflation penalty condition is sharpened to a necessary-and-sufficient threshold, with a Davis-Kahan bound quantifying effects of approximate projectors. Numerical studies separate mapping correctness, ansatz expressibility, preprocessing, Pauli growth, finite-shot uncertainty, and damage localization. For 128-DOF chains, consistent-mass whitening increases transformed-operator density from 0.023 to 0.308 and Pauli terms from 576 to 2950. Exact state-vector experiments show qubit count and circuit expressibility are distinct. At 10^5 shots per Pauli term, first-mode frequency RMS error is 2.45%. In an oracle-state study, 10% stiffness loss is localized in 84.5% of trials. Results sharpen the deflation condition, quantify resource bottlenecks, and claim no speedup.

items.title: Nonlinear quantum noise polarization in macroscopic nonlinear QED
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Arman Kashef, Stefan Scheel, Marco Ornigotti
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a quantum theory of light in nonlinearly responding materials with dispersion and absorption and, in particular, show the emergence of non-Gaussian noise associated with nonlinear absorption processes. Our theory is based on a path-integral formulation of the microscopic Huttner-Barnett model including cubic matter self-interaction required for $\chi^{(2)}$ nonlinear processes. We show that the noise polarization emerges naturally from a decoupling of the stochastic weights of the bath response which, in case of cubic self-interactions, leads to a decoupling via Airy functions. As the theory is, by construction, consistent with the nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem, it constitutes a viable quantum theory of light in nonlinear media.

items.title: ConQEC: Concolic Testing for Quantum Error-Correcting Code Implementations
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Zihao Li, Ji Guan, Mingsheng Ying
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum error-correcting code (QECC) implementations are hybrid software-control systems: measured syndromes drive decoder dispatch, recovery actions, and logical checks. Existing QECC verification techniques can prove formal obligations, and general quantum testing can expose final failures, but developers still lack a scalable testing workflow that generates concrete faults and explains where a QECC repair path first diverges. This paper presents ConQEC, to our knowledge the first concolic testing framework for QECC implementations. By combining concrete (Pauli) fault replay with symbolic repair-path constraints, ConQEC generates tests that expose not only final logical failures but also fault--syndrome--decoder--recovery (FSDR) diagnostics: the injected fault, observed syndrome, decoder decision, recovery action, oracle result, and earliest divergent stage. Its symbolic encoding of Pauli faults, syndrome predicates, decoder and recovery relations, and oracle checks enables this diagnostic workflow to scale beyond exponentially increasing amplitude-level quantum-state reasoning. We implemented ConQEC and evaluated it on generated source-level QECC families and public QECC artifacts with up to thousands of qubits. items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Yoshihiko Abe, Ryo Nagai
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent (QCHD), a continuous-time quantum framework for optimization under smooth equality constraints. The unconstrained counterpart, Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD), minimizes a cost function by simulating the Schr\"odinger dynamics of a particle in the potential given by the cost function. Applying Dirac's formalism to the classical dynamics with constraints, we construct an intrinsic quantum Hamiltonian with a Laplace--Beltrami operator on the constraint manifold in a kinetic term. Its evolution preserves the constraints exactly without penalty terms and is expected to solve quantum-dynamically the constrained optimization problem. We analyze its relation to Quantum Hamiltonian Descent supplemented by a strong penalty term. For a squared-distance penalty, the effective tangential dynamics acquires an extrinsic-curvature potential and, in nontrivial normal-rotation sectors, a coupling to the normal-bundle connection. These embedding-dependent terms remain in the strong-penalty limit, generally yielding quantum dynamics different from QCHD. Numerical comparisons for circular, elliptical, and two simultaneous constraints show faster optimization and improved concentration near global minima for the initial states and finite penalty strengths considered.

items.title: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Philipp Stammer
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of entangled quantum optical states in high-harmonic generation raises a fundamental problem about its characterization, namely, \textit{how can entanglement of extreme-ultraviolet radiation be certified for attosecond light fields?} Here, we provide experimentally accessible separability tests, particularly showing that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides a direct solution to this problem. This is achieved by a quantum optical treatment of mapping photoelectron interferometry to the measurement of optical correlation functions. This yields a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements. We evaluate both witnesses on explicit optical states and identify how the protocol can be extended to XUV-XUV entanglement certification. Hence, we establish attosecond photoelectron interferometry as a general framework for entanglement certification across a wide range of optical frequencies.

items.title: Local Dephasing Sustains Continuous Time Crystals in a Spin-1/2 Ensemble
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Zhen-huan Yang, Dan-Bo Zhang
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local pure dephasing suppresses single-spin coherence, yet we show that it sustains continuous time-crystalline order in a fully connected ferromagnetic spin-$1/2$ ensemble with local decay. An exact operator identity reveals the mechanism: dephasing raises the interaction energy, while energy relaxation on a finite timescale converts this charging into delayed feedback. Within homogeneous mean-field theory, we prove that dephasing is necessary for periodic motion in this model and that feedback exactly balances transverse damping over each cycle. Beyond mean field, the identity fixes the relative amplitude and phase of energy and longitudinal magnetization in oscillatory Liouvillian modes. Liouvillian spectra and stationary two-time correlations characterize temporal order through decay rates that decrease algebraically with system size, frequencies approaching nonzero mean-field values, and comparable per-spin oscillatory weights. Semiclassical trajectories further reveal recurrent switching between a limit-cycle region and two symmetry-related stationary regions: fluctuations interrupt and reactivate collective oscillations, and oscillatory episodes provide an intermediate channel between stationary regions. These results establish local dephasing as a resource for autonomous collective motion and show how the resulting temporal order can participate in metastable dynamics.

items.title: Fluctuation-free Quantum Battery Charging Enabled by Bell-like Entangled and Separable Charger States
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Longyan Gong, Jing Zhang, Yongtao Li
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The implication of entanglement in quantum battery charging remains poorly understood. In addition, intrinsic quantum randomness poses a fundamental challenge to charging uniformity across distinct trials. To address these issues, we study a three-qubit system within a cascaded collision frame, with two qubits acting as the charger and the third serving as the battery. After each collision, an adaptive measurement is performed on the charger, yielding four conditional post-measurement battery states with identical expected stored energy. For arbitrary fixed charger states, we derive analytical expressions for the recurrence relation of stored energy. We find that stored-energy fluctuations depend on whether the dynamics relies on the battery phase \(\gamma_n\). For two Bell-like families of entangled states, together with their computational basis states termed Bell-like separable states, the dynamics is \(\gamma_n\)-independent and fluctuations vanish, whereas for other entangled and separable states, fluctuations emerge. These insights establish a paradigm for engineering charger states to design uniform-charging quantum-battery architectures despite inherent quantum randomness.

items.title: Reset-Enhanced Dissipative Quantum Metrology
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Silan Li, Qingjun Tong, Ruicheng Bao
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum metrology is ultimately shaped not only by measurements, but also by the dissipative dynamics that prepare and maintain the probe. Nevertheless, a general mechanism for enhancing both steady-state and transient precision in open quantum systems has been lacking. Here we show that adding a simple reset channel provides such a mechanism: reset acts as a minimal dissipative control that can enhance metrological precision without modifying the intrinsic Hamiltonian or applying continuous coherent driving. We derive a unified quantum-Fisher-information (QFI) reset-rate response identity, showing how reset enhances steady-state and transient estimation while revealing a sharp transient distinction. For static-parameter estimation in diagonal dynamics, reset leaves the leading short-time QFI unchanged; for the separate task of elapsed-time estimation, it generates an immediate drift contribution that can scale quadratically with the reset rate in the short-time limit. For frequency estimation, the enhancement is instead dominated by a genuinely quantum eigenvector contribution. These results establish reset as a simple dissipative resource for open-system quantum metrology.

items.title: Can Entanglement-Induced Feature-Map Designs Improve Projected Quantum Kernels?
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Ravi Kumar Jha, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Projected quantum kernels (PQKs) have emerged as a notable approach to circumvent the hardness of machine learning tasks arising from the exponential dimensionality of the quantum Hilbert space. However, recent PQK studies often rely heavily on extensive classical hyperparameter tuning of the radial basis function (RBF) kernel parameter and the support vector machine regularization parameter. The extensive tuning can mask the true representational power of the underlying PQKs induced by quantum feature maps, which has not been explored in detail. Thus, this work aims to expose the structural capabilities of PQKs by isolating and evaluating their native inductive bias through comparisons between untuned and tuned PQKs against the RBF baseline. Furthermore, we propose novel quantum feature maps that leverage two-qubit entanglement to capture multivariate correlations in IoT data. The results show that extensive tuning can lead to competitive performance architectures, while our proposed entanglement topologies exhibit a significantly stronger native inductive bias. This reveals that superior quantum architectural design can yield structurally better PQKs with improvements arising from quantum-mechanical properties rather than from classical hyperparameter tuning.

items.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. II. System-parameter uncertainties and overall errors
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Chia-Hsien Huang, Hsi-Sheng Goan
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the companion paper (Part I), we developed an optimal-control framework to suppress intrinsic and decoherence-induced errors in controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons. Here, we extend this framework to incorporate uncertainties in coupling strength, anharmonicities, and zero-flux qubit frequencies, enabling the design of high-fidelity gates robust against noise and parameter uncertainties. We classify these uncertainties by whether they perturb the off-diagonal coupling strengths or the diagonal detunings of the Hamiltonian, and we identify distinct suppression mechanisms for each class. Coupling errors are mitigated through dynamical decoupling induced by strong detuning modulation. For a 30-ns gate, this strategy reduces the coupling error to $6.21\times10^{-7}$ and tolerates coupling-strength uncertainties up to $2\pi\times4$ MHz while keeping total gate infidelity below $10^{-3}$. Detuning errors are minimized near a symmetric-detuning operating point that balances the two dominant leakage-mediated interactions. A 24-ns gate operated near this point tolerates individual uncertainties of up to $2\pi\times5$ MHz in each relevant diagonal parameter under the same infidelity threshold. We further optimize gate performance under realistic conditions where intrinsic errors, decoherence, and parameter uncertainties coexist across six representative stages of progressively improving hardware performance. The resulting stage-specific controls achieve lower infidelity and greater robustness. Together with the companion study (Part I), this framework offers a practical approach to balance speed, fidelity, and robustness while reducing the need for exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

items.title: Time-reversal-based quantum metrology in a central-spin architecture: from SATIN to butterfly echo
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Aditya Kumar, Sayan Choudhury
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced time-reversal-based metrology using the central spin model, in which a single ancilla spin of magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ mediates interactions between $N$ bath spins through a star-graph topology. We demonstrate that the SATIN (Signal Amplification Through Time-reversal Interaction) echo protocol can be implemented in this setup to achieve a Fisher information of $N^2/e$ with the collective $\langle J_y\rangle$ readout, corresponding to a $4.34\,\mathrm{dB}$ offset from the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we establish that this platform provides a pathway to perform the butterfly echo protocol by conjugating each evolution step with a random collective bath rotation, thereby achieving axis-agnostic Heisenberg-scaled sensing. Crucially, with a small $N-$independent number of random steps, the butterfly echo reaches a Fisher information of $N^2/4$ ($6\,\mathrm{dB}$ below the Heisenberg limit) for any unknown encoding axis, with the plateau gain tracking the Haar limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the central-spin magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ provides a powerful knob to reduce the optimal protocol timescale without altering the metrological ceiling or the circuit depth required to reach isotropy. The proposed scheme is relevant to cavity QED and NMR quantum processors, where the central spin architecture arises naturally.

items.title: Demand-Driven Routing Space for Lattice-Surgery Compilation
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Hanyu Wang, Wan-Hsuan Lin, Zihan Chen, Eddy Z. Zhang, Jason Cong
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lattice-surgery compilation places logical qubits on a grid of surface-code tiles and routes their interactions. Sparse static layouts limit routing contention but reserve space that often remains idle. Reducing this reservation requires balancing area savings against additional gate serialization and qubit movement. In this paper, we present a co-designed dynamic architecture and compiler that allocates routing space according to circuit demand. The architecture preserves a fixed virtual qubit floorplan while allowing its physical spacing to change between execution stages. The compiler coordinates placement, scheduling, and routing to implement lattice surgeries using fewer physical qubits. Across our application benchmarks, our method reduces space-time volume by 55.6% in geometric mean and compiles 75.5 times faster than the evaluated DasCot configuration. A circuit-synthesis case study shows how our compiler exposes optimization tradeoffs.

items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Anurag Anshu, Quynh T. Nguyen
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Port-based teleportation (PBT) is a variant of quantum teleportation that does not require corrections on the teleported state: starting with $N$ shared EPR states, Alice can teleport a qudit to Bob by performing a measurement on her system and informing Bob which of his $N$ `ports' to retrieve the state, up to infidelity decaying with $N$. Existing quantum circuits of PBT rely on representation theory tools and the mixed Schur transform. In this note, we report an elementary efficient circuit for PBT, which has depth $\operatorname{polylog}(N,d)$. As a corollary, this gives a simple proof that all $n$-qubit unitaries can be parallelized to $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ depth, recovering a recent result due to Nehoran--Slote--Yuen and OpenAI.

items.title: Exceptional point structure and chiral state transfer in a rate-operator-engineered $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Bose-Hubbard dimer
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Jaakko Luomala, Federico Settimo, Kimmo Luoma, Iiro Vilja, Jyrki Piilo
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rate operator quantum jumps (ROQJ) is a general method to unravel a master equation describing the dynamics of an open quantum system into stochastic pure state trajectories. By post-selecting on no jumps occurring, one obtains a trajectory generated by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. The ROQJ allows for versatile modification of this non-Hermitian evolution, with each non-Hermitian Hamiltonian corresponding to a different continuous measurement scheme. We apply the ROQJ to modify the non-Hermitian dynamics of the open three-particle Bose-Hubbard dimer model under environmental non-local dephasing to construct a $PT$-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonians with a general two parameter $PT$-symmetric imaginary diagonal part, which generalizes the well-known gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. We characterize the symmetry structure of the spectrum for different on-site interaction strengths. For vanishing on-site interaction, we find the unbroken $PT$-symmetry region enclosed by order two exceptional lines of different character and four order four exceptional points, two of which are not found in the usual gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. Additionally, we find regions with degenerate imaginary parts of the eigenvalues, also not found in the gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. In this parameter space, we use time-dependent rate operator transformations to investigate state transfer under slowly varying parameter loops. Loops encircling an order four exceptional point exhibit chiral state transfer. Because the loops cross exceptional lines, the final states are superpositions of eigenstates. Chiral state transfer is also found with non-zero homogeneous on-site interaction when the loop crosses over broken $PT$-symmetry regions of different character. Using inhomogeneous on-site interactions, we find direction dependent state transfer between eigenstates without crossing or encircling exceptional points.

items.title: Noise redistribution by stabilizer codes: an organizing view of concatenated three-qubit codes
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Long Huang
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an organizing framework for concatenated quantum error correction based on the observation that the syndrome projection of a stabilizer code reshapes the noise channel in a code-determined manner. For any stabilizer code, one level of QEC maps the physical noise to a block-diagonal logical channel whose diagonal Pauli weights are fixed by the code geometry. Coherences between different syndrome classes vanish, and no physical Pauli twirl is required to reach this block-diagonal form. Concatenation can then be viewed as the iteration of the same redistribution step: the dominant logical error after one level selects the code used at the next. We instantiate the framework with the two smallest stabilizer codes, the bit-flip and phase-flip codes, and apply it to amplitude damping. The redistribution rules give the concatenation protocol $C_2(\hat\sigma_y) C_1(\hat\sigma_x)$, whose ideal-recovery fidelity scales as $f_l=1-\mathcal O(\gamma^2)$. Solving the crossover condition $F_l>F_{l-1}$ in the ideal-gate limit yields a critical damping parameter $\gamma_c\approx0.30$; in terms of the initial channel fidelity, $f=1-1.72755\gamma^2$. Under the same ideal-recovery assumption, we compare the overall gate accuracy rate with that of the five-qubit code. The scope of the framework, in particular for coherent and correlated noise, is stated explicitly.

items.title: Scale-free localization in pseudo-Hermitian quantum walk
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Haiting Zhang, Lei Xiao, Cui-Xian Guo, Quan Lin, Peng Xue
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scale-free localization is a distinctive phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems, where specific eigenstates, known as scale-free localized states (LSs), possess localization lengths that scale linearly with the system size. Here, we show that a single non-Hermitian defect in one-dimensional quantum walks (QWs) induces scale-free localization. Driven by non-Hermiticity, the QW system undergoes a pseudo-Hermitian (PH) phase transition and the PH symmetry breaking is accompanied by the emergence of scale-free localization. As non-Hermiticity is further increased, the system undergoes a second phase transition, marked by the emergence of two pairs of bound states. Crucially, we identify the critical points of both transitions using localization properties. Furthermore, we extend our investigation to two-dimensional QWs, where a single non-Hermitian defect also induces scale-free localization, thereby demonstrating the universality of this phenomenon. Our work provides a valuable perspective for further exploring defect physics and a type of novel LS in non-Hermitian quantum systems.

items.title: Norm-Aware Product Formulas for Hamiltonian Simulations
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Carlos A. Pi\~neiro Moreno, Pascal Krause, Annika Bande
items.summary: arXiv:2610.31070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the target of efficiently solving the quantum-mechanical Schr\"odinger equation on future quantum computers, first- and second-order product formulas for the time-evolution operator are proposed, designed to exploit hierarchies in the operator norms of the individual Hamiltonian components. Inspired by the THRIFT product formula, these decomposition schemes achieve a suppression of the leading error term by a factor of alpha<1 with respect to the standard Lie--Trotter--Suzuki splitting of the same order, where alpha quantifies the norm ratio between the dominant and subdominant parts of the Hamiltonian. Unlike THRIFT, the proposed formulas retain the general product-formula structure, making them applicable to Hamiltonians whose terms act on an arbitrary number of qubits. The advantages of this approach are demonstrated through numerical experiments on engineered two-dimensional spin-1/2 XY model systems and isolated molecules within the double-factorization framework.

items.title: On the Role of Problem Structure in Single-Layer QAOA
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Guilherme Adamatti Bridi, Franklin de Lima Marquezino, Andris Ambainis
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Problem structure is regarded as a key factor influencing the performance of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), yet it remains an informal notion without a precise mathematical characterization. In this work, we address this issue by identifying a mathematical object that captures problem structure as seen from the perspective of the target state amplitude in single-layer QAOA. Specifically, we show that this structure is encoded in a joint probability distribution induced by the unique coarsest partition of the computational basis, determined by problem cost values and mixer-dependent walk counts. The statistical dependence between these classes provides a means of quantifying the available problem structure and identifying necessary conditions for exponential amplification. To assess the extent to which this structure can translate into algorithmic performance, we establish a mean-max non-separation bound relating the parameter-averaged probability of measuring the target configuration to its variational maximum. For NPO-PB problems with polynomially many distinct mixer eigenvalues, these probabilities exhibit the same scaling up to polynomial factors. This allows us to characterize the exponential scaling of optimal amplitude amplification by analyzing the parameter-averaged probability without explicitly optimizing the variational parameters. We then derive an exact expression for the parameter-averaged probability as a matrix inner product involving two objects that separately encode the joint structural distribution and the mixer dynamics. This representation provides a framework for identifying the structural mechanisms governing the amplification of the target-state probability or its exponential suppression relative to the mixer capacity. We demonstrate these mechanisms through analytically tractable examples involving transverse field and Grover mixers.

items.title: Probing quasiperiodic spectral accessibility with a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Shujie Cheng, Lucas C. C\'eleri, Norton G. de Almeida, Gao Xianlong, G. D. de Moraes Neto
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasiperiodic systems combine sharply different spectral and localisation regimes with a dense hierarchy of dynamical time scales. We show that a finite-rate quantum Otto cycle can use this structure as a thermodynamic probe, revealing which parts of the spectrum become dynamically accessible and thermodynamically relevant during a driven transformation. For a generalised Aubry-Andr\'e-Harper chain, the resulting response is not determined by the static quasiperiodic regime alone: extended, near-critical, and crossing protocols do not exhibit universal ordering of work fluctuations. Instead, the statistics reflect transition pathways that are simultaneously dynamically coupled, thermally occupied, and energetically significant. The same spectral accessibility separates thermodynamic recovery from microscopic adiabatic recovery. Positive mean work can reappear while the population transfer dynamics remain strongly nonadiabatic because finite-rate population transfer is redistributed toward energetically less costly channels rather than suppressed. The full work distribution reveals a further separation, with a finite rate window in which positive-work cycles form a majority although the mean work remains negative. This behaviour persists in finite-size analysis. A thermally weighted spectral susceptibility connects these effects to a distributed hierarchy of dynamically active spectral regions rather than to a single minimum-gap bottleneck. Finite thermal contacts preserve this picture while introducing a second time scale and intercycle memory. Quantum Otto cycles can therefore provide a fluctuation-resolved thermodynamic probe of quasiperiodic spectral accessibility, complementary to direct spectroscopic and eigenstate-resolved diagnostics.

items.title: Mode-Selective Micromotion Compensation via Coherent Excitation of a Ground-State-Cooled Motional Mode
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Tetsu Kinase, Ippei Nakamura, Atsushi Noguchi
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Excess micromotion induced by stray DC electric fields limits the control fidelity of trapped-ion experiments. Various techniques have been developed to detect and compensate ion displacements from the RF null by monitoring modulated fluorescence, ion positions, or micromotion sidebands. Although these approaches are effective, they do not probe the displacement through a ground-state-cooled motional mode and therefore offer limited compatibility with quantum-enhanced sensing protocols. Here, we demonstrate a micromotion compensation method based on the driven coherent amplitude of a ground-state-cooled motional mode. In this approach, the ion displacement is converted into a coherent motional excitation by an auxiliary RF drive and detected through the qubit. We determine the optimal compensation field with a $1\sigma$ statistical uncertainty of 8 mV/m. The method is naturally compatible with quantum-enhanced sensing protocols employing nonclassical motional states, including Fock, squeezed, and Schr\"odinger-cat states, providing a pathway toward quantum-enhanced micromotion compensation.

items.title: On the Structure of Quantum Finite-Level Systems: Decoherence-Free Subsystems, Quantum Nondemolition Variables, and Back-Action-Evading Measurements
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Jia Gu, Guofeng Zhang, Ian R. Petersen
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to conduct a comprehensive structural analysis of quantum finite-level systems in the Heisenberg picture, where the evolution of system observables is modeled by bilinear quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). Firstly, real coordinate transformations that preserve commutation and anticommutation relations are characterized, and relative admissibility between different orthonormal Hermitian bases is formulated. Secondly, strongly aligned subspaces are introduced, based on which decoherence-free subsystems (DFSs) are constructed in general orthonormal Hermitian basis as well as the generalized Gell-Mann basis. Thirdly, conditions for the existence of quantum nondemolition (QND) variables are given in terms of both linear systems theory and spectral separation by output-signal observables. Finally, a sufficient condition for quantum back-action-evading (BAE) measurements is established. A four-qubit nearest-neighbor Heisenberg chain with collective dephasing illustrates these structural properties of quantum finite-level systems.

items.title: Coherence and imaginarity of qubit states under vanishing Bargmann invariants
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Hao-Fan Wang, Lin Chen
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Set coherence and set imaginarity are two important quantum resources defined by sets of states. We investigate tuples of qubit states under vanishing higher-order Bargmann invariants and show that their set coherence and set imaginarity are each related to whether they contain a pair of orthogonal states. Specifically, when the relevant higher-order Bargmann invariants vanish, the tuple contains a pair of orthogonal states if and only if removing some state makes the remaining tuple incoherent. Moreover, when maximally mixed states are excluded, the same vanishing conditions imply that the tuple is imaginarity-free if and only if it contains a pair of orthogonal states. As a consequence, under these conditions, a tuple of single-qubit states has imaginarity precisely when every tuple obtained by deleting one of its states is coherent.

items.title: FVQKD: A Formal Verification of Quantum Key Distribution Security in Rocq
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Ruixuan Deng, Zhengfeng Ji, Jiayu Zhang, Li Zhou
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD), whose security is derived from quantum mechanics rather than computational assumptions, is moving into standardization and commercial deployment. Yet its security guarantees rest on technically delicate proofs checked by hand. Formal verification closes this gap, establishing a two-factor assurance: unconditional security from physical principles, and machine-checked proofs against reasoning errors. We present FVQKD, a Rocq library for machine-checking QKD security proofs. Its first result is a complete, end-to-end machine-checked proof of composable, finite-key security for BB84. The mechanization reconstructs the complete proof infrastructure from first principles, including the smooth entropy framework, the entropic uncertainty relation, and the Quantum Leftover Hash Lemma. It uncovers necessary side conditions that the published argument leaves unstated, one of which reveals a missing proof branch, and it grounds the information-theoretic bound in a formal semantics of protocol execution, which the pen-and-paper analysis lacks. The proof is entirely admit-free, relying only on the Rocq kernel and standard foundational axioms. To our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end formal verification of a QKD security proof. Built on MathComp, MathComp-Analysis, and CoqQ, the development provides quantum-information infrastructure designed for reuse across broader QKD variants and quantum cryptography applications.

items.title: Dealing with low-weight errors that lead BP OSD to fail
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Giacomo Fregona, Matthias C. L\"obl, Benjamin J. Brown, Michael J. Kastoryano, Stefano Paesani
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Belief Propagation combined with Ordered Statistics Decoding (BP OSD) is an open-source decoding tool used widely within the community due to its versatility and ease of application to Quantum Low Density Parity Check (QLDPC) codes. However, the degeneracy of quantum codes has been observed to degrade the performance of BP OSD, particularly leading to error floors for low physical error rates. Here, we investigate the low-weight error configurations responsible for such failures in Bivariate Bicycle codes. We show that, at code capacity, BP OSD fails on errors whose weight is significantly smaller than d/2, arising from global symmetries of the decoding graph that prevent the convergence of parallel BP. Furthermore, our analysis reveals new pitfalls that can arise when analysing the performance of BP OSD in the rare events regime, such as loss of ergodicity in splitting methods and numerical instabilities in the decoder. We show how to mitigate these failure mechanisms by modifying the BP update rules and the decoder implementation, leading to substantial improvement in logical error rate.

items.title: Normal-Form Characterization of Adaptivity and Entanglement in Pauli-Based Computation
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Filipa C. R. Peres, Selman Ipek, Daniel Lovsted, Joshua Nevin, Anne Broadbent
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pauli-based computation (PBC) is a measurement-based model of quantum computation that samples from output distributions of universal Clifford+$T$ circuits. Here, we provide a normal form (NF) that completely characterizes its adaptive and entanglement structures. These insights unify PBC with one-way quantum computing as dual or `time-reversed' counterparts. We use the NF to advance strategies for distributed computation and investigate magic-state injection rates. We also demonstrate an exponential improvement in the detection of unnecessary magic-state qubits, allowing their efficient removal. Our NF further enables ahead-of-time circuit compilation using PBC, reducing CNOT gate count and quantum memory of random quantum circuits on average by 50% and 40%, respectively, beating other state-of-the-art compilers.

items.summary: arXiv:2610.30375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Group IV color centers in diamond -- silicon, germanium, tin, and lead-vacancy centers -- are a promising platform for quantum networking. Typical Group-IV creation utilizes ion implantation during diamond growth that leaves the color centers with a broad depth distribution and damage-induced strain inhomogeneity. Deterministic placement and damage reduction in Group IV generation are essential for improving this platform. In this letter, we report on the localization of germanium-vacancy (GeV$^-$) to a $<$ 10 nm layer via the timed injection of GeH$_4$ during microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition. In this layer we have realized 17 ppm of Ge and a strain-free environment for the GeV$^-$. Subsequent electron irradiation and annealing have generated a sheet density of 0.12 GeV$^-$/$\mu$m$^2$. The minimal damage from color center generation mitigates spectral inhomogeneity and allows spectral resolution of isotopic clusters, with the best cluster having an inhomogeneous distribution of 2.14 GHz and an average linewidth of $47 \pm 11$ MHz. Our study gives insight into formation dynamics of GeV$^-$ in delta-doped systems and estimates our vacancy to GeV$^-$ yield to be $\geq$ 90%, establishing an athermal nearest-neighbor formation model. We further characterized the spin $T_2^*$ and set a lower bound of 730 ns, limited by a paramagnetic defect.

items.title: Memory--Transport Competition in Physical Two-Bath Quantum Reset Dynamics
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Jishad Kumar, Achilleas Lazarides, Tapio Ala-Nissila
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherence preservation and environmental renewal offer competing ways of controlling quantum memory and transport. We show that a seemingly natural protocol which exactly replaces the bath occupations while preserving arbitrary system--bath coherences need not correspond to a physical fermionic state. We instead construct a two-reservoir protocol with independent, number-conserving thermal attenuators, for which complete positivity and fermionic admissibility hold by construction. Physical attenuation necessarily modifies bath populations as well as cross correlations; the coherence control is not an independent hard-reset knob. Quadratic dynamics reduces the stroboscopic problem to an exact matrix fixed-point equation without a weak-coupling or Markov approximation. Analytically, coherence retention enhances the leading short-cycle transfer rate, including the complete-erasure limit; no general endpoint-vanishing theorem exists. An exact stationary continuity theorem forces the through-current to vanish whenever either reservoir is left entirely unrefreshed, although no analogous theorem suppresses it at complete erasure. For biased structured reservoirs, exact finite-chain calculations display distinct coherence-, current-, and signed energy-transfer operating points; a resolved high-retention boundary layer exposes strong finite-size sensitivity of the coherence peak. The model provides a microscopic, fermion-admissible benchmark for the interplay of reservoir coherence, particle transport, and energetic exchange.

items.author: Haowei Shi, Kartikeya Arora, Zheshen Zhang, Quntao Zhuang
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose distributed dual-comb spectroscopy, a quantum-enhanced sensing architecture that simultaneously exploits spatial- and spectral-domain entanglement to improve the extraction of global spectroscopic information across broadband frequency ranges. Our scheme consists of a network of Mach-Zehnder interferometers interrogating spatially separated samples, each driven by a classical frequency comb at the bright port. A single two-mode squeezed frequency comb is distributed through a passive beam-splitter array into $K$ entangled combs, establishing multipartite correlations across sensors while preserving intrinsic spectral entanglement. The protocol is compatible with both heterodyne detection and division detection, and enables parallel estimation of weighted-average absorption features over multiple frequency components. Compared with spatially separable quantum strategies requiring $K$ independently engineered nonclassical comb sources, our approach achieves enhanced signal-to-noise performance using only a single quantum resource distributed across the network. These results establish a scalable route toward broadband distributed quantum spectroscopy with simultaneous spatial and spectral advantage.

items.title: Photon localization: Local measurements, localized states, and causality
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Jan Gulla, Johannes Skaar
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review what it means for a relativistic particle to be localized and argue that the most useful approach is through local measurement. This perspective ties localization directly to relativistic causality and measurable outcomes in spacetime. Strict localization in quantum field theory is formalized by states that give the same expectation value as vacuum for all local observables outside some spacetime region. With this formalism, single photons cannot be strictly localized, but coherent states can. The structure and interpretation of local observables and local operator algebras are discussed in connection with the Reeh-Schlieder theorem. Since probabilities of local measurement outcomes cannot vanish in vacuum, particle detection events must be phrased carefully. Key characteristics of strictly localized states are surveyed alongside concrete strategies for constructing them. The relationship between localization, causality, and on-demand sources is analyzed, finding that strictly localized states can represent localized, propagating information in quantum field theory. Explicit examples of localized photonic states are presented with an emphasis on quantum optics, including states that approximate single photons and (entangled) Bell states.

items.title: Scalable Neural Wave Functions via Information Mixing and Hierarchical Network Architectures
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Faith Oyedemi, Stefanie Czischek
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Numerically simulating quantum many-body systems is one of the central challenges in modern physics, as the exponential growth of the Hilbert space with system size renders large-scale exact solutions intractable. Over the past decade, generative artificial neural networks have emerged as powerful wave function ans\"atze that have powered advances in finding ground state representations, reconstructing quantum states from data, and modeling dynamics in quantum many-body systems. While recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are computationally efficient, the recurrent nature can limit their capacity to capture long-range correlations. Transformer models with their underlying self-attention mechanism excel at capturing these long-range correlations, but incur increased computational requirements, restricting applications to small physical systems. In this work, we address these limitations by exploring the multi-layer perceptron (MLP) mixer model as a wave function ansatz. By mixing information globally and locally through the system via a computationally lightweight mixing strategy, this architecture promises to combine the ability to capture long-range correlations with low computational costs. We benchmark the model on finding ground state representations of two-dimensional quantum many-body systems in various phases of matter and investigate the behavior of representational accuracy and computational efficiency for different physical system sizes. By comparing its performance to RNNs and transformer models with single-site and patched input definitions, we demonstrate that the MLP mixer architecture performs competitively with state-of-the-art network models. We further show that a hierarchical combination of this model with the transformer model outperforms other state-of-the-art architectures for large-scale quantum systems, opening new avenues for investigating quantum phases of matter.

items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Miles D. Gorman
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant syndrome extraction is fundamental to stabilizer-code-based quantum error correction, yet existing general protocols incur substantial costs in either circuit depth or width. In this work, we design ancilla stabilizer states for a general transversal circuit to construct a family of fault-tolerant syndrome-extraction gadgets that interpolate between Shor and Steane syndrome extraction for any stabilizer code. The result is a configurable trade-off between circuit depth and width.

items.title: Pure states are optimal for total energy-constrained quantum channel discrimination
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Christos N. Gagatsos
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the discrimination of two quantum channels acting on bosonic modes, with a probe state of fixed mean photon number and no ancilla. We prove that pure probes are optimal: for every mixed probe there is a pure probe with exactly the same mean photon number that performs at least as well. The result holds for arbitrary channels and for every figure of merit built from the Chernoff quantities $\Tr[\rho_1^s\rho_2^{1-s}]$, including the quantum Chernoff exponent, as well as for the single-shot error probability. The proof relies on a decomposition of any state of mean photon number $\nb$ into pure states of mean photon number exactly $\nb$, which extends a matrix rank-one decomposition of Huang and Zhang to density operators of infinite rank.

items.title: Lean-QuantumAlg: A Framework for AI Agents to Produce Quantum Algorithms that Humans Can Trust
items.subtitle: ARXIV · QUANT-PH · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Lei Zhang, Mingrui Jing, Yusheng Zhao, Jiahong Liu, Xin Wang
items.summary: arXiv:2610.30216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are increasingly capable of constructing quantum algorithms and proofs, yet machine-checked proofs alone cannot guarantee that the intended problem is solved or that resource claims match the verified computation.Here we introduce Lean-QuantumAlg, a Lean 4 framework for trustworthy AI-assisted development of quantum algorithms.Its Algorithm-Solves-Problem contract binds correctness, success probability, borrowed-state restoration and quantum and classical resource bounds to a single execution, while separating the guarantees that Lean checks from the problem specifications and execution models that humans review. We demonstrate the framework on nine AI-formalized quantum algorithms, from Grover search to quantum attacks on RSA-2048 and P-256, with less than 1% of each algorithm's imported source code requiring statement-level human review once the shared framework has been audited. By integrating reusable mathematical foundations, certified algorithmic primitives and execution-grounded verification, Lean-QuantumAlg provides a basis for AI agents to construct and certify quantum algorithms, opening a path toward scalable AI-driven discovery of quantum algorithms.

items.title: Why Testing Structural Theories Requires the Unconscious Condition
items.subtitle: PSYARXIV · 精神分析 · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Zefan Zheng, João Pedro Parreira Rodrigues, Lukas Kob, Karla Matić
items.summary: Consciousness science has traditionally proceeded by contrasting neural activity when a stimulus is consciously perceived against activity when the same stimulus is not perceived. This contrastive approach is well suited to locating neural correlates of consciousness, but it says little about why an experience has the particular character it does. A recent structural turn addresses this gap by comparing the relational structure of qualia with the relational structure of a candidate physical substrate. We review the main structure-matching programmes and what they offer beyond the contrastive approach. We then argue that all of them rest on an assumption that has never been tested directly, which we call the structural exclusivity assumption: That a neural structure matching the qualia structure reflects the neural substrate of consciousness itself, rather than merely the processing of information that can occur without conscious experience. The assumption is empirical rather than philosophical, and the standard structure-matching design cannot test it, because qualia and physical structures are estimated while the content is consciously perceived. We set out the design that would test it, and review the psychophysical and neural evidence currently bearing on it. That evidence consistently suggests that relational structure survives absence of awareness, though no existing study settles the question. We argue that structure-matching and contrastive designs must be combined, and consider what follows for the selection of candidate structures and for the promise of the dissolution of the hard problem of consciousness.

items.title: Unconscious Archetypal Selection Bias in Professional Ice Hockey: A Multivariate Positional Analysis of Astrological Ephemeris Data and the Relative Age Effect
items.subtitle: PSYARXIV · 精神分析 · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: David R. Juillet, Jorge M. Rodrigues, Joanne V. Longtin
items.summary: This study investigates whether unconscious scouting bias exists in National Hockey League (NHL) talent acquisition, driven by psychological and behavioral archetypes. Analyzing a dataset of 777 players across all 32 NHL rosters, the research quantifies standard physical maturity biases, such as the Relative Age Effect (RAE), against independent lunar variables (Sign, Element, Modality) mapped to emotional typologies. Utilizing exact binomial tests, Cohen’s h effect sizes, and Savage-Dickey Bayes Factors (B10), 4,864 distinct positional configurations were evaluated. Results indicate no archetypal solar advantage capable of overcoming the RAE physical penalty. However, when evaluating independent lunar placements across specific positional subgroups (e.g., Centers, Left Wings, Right Wings, Defensemen), extreme localized scouting biases emerge. Front offices consistently filter players through highly distinct, positional psychological profiles, with 13 franchises exhibiting three or more concurrent statistical anomalies, indicating that human evaluation networks unconsciously draft for specific behavioral mechanics.

items.author: Matthias Pillny, Stefan Leucht, Björn Schlier
items.summary: Montag and colleagues report a randomised trial of modified psychodynamic psychotherapy for schizophrenia (MPP-S) plus treatment as usual (TAU) versus TAU alone. We welcome efforts to strengthen the evidence base for psychodynamic psychotherapy. Given the limited access to psychological treatment for people with psychosis and the, at best, moderate effects of existing pharmacological and psychological interventions this is a valuable effort to advance evidence-based treatment in psychosis. Several methodological decisions, however, complicate interpretation of its findings.

items.title: Representations of Change Support Object Individuation in Infancy
items.subtitle: PSYARXIV · 分析心理学 · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Peter Mazalik, Justin Halberda
items.summary: “One can never step in the same river twice, for it is not the same river and he is not the same man.” This ancient puzzle by Heraclitus highlights that the world, and ourselves, are constantly changing. But to raise these puzzles, one must engage the concept of CHANGE. Developmental research shows that even infants represent highly abstract notions, including objects, agents, cause, and number. Here, we ask whether they also represent CHANGE.We adapted the individuation paradigm pioneered by Xu and Carey (1996), in which two objects emerge sequentially from behind an occluder, preventing spatiotemporal cues about the number of objects. Infants must instead rely on contrastive featural/kind information. Prior work shows that before 12 months, infants fail to individuate objects differing in basic-level category (e.g., duck vs. truck), but succeed with broader distinctions (e.g., object vs. agent).Here we show that infants can use the contrast between a continuously changing object and a static object to infer the number of entities present. This effect cannot beexplained by saliency alone, as infants’ longer looking at unexpected outcomes differsfrom any preference for the more salient changing object, and is striking in light ofreports that infants at this age fail to individuate objects by color alone (Leslie, 1998).Representing change opens a new avenue for research: What types of change areencoded? Over what timescales? Embedded in which cognitive systems? By 8 months,infants already appreciate change as a core property of the world.

items.title: Reframing the Unconscious: A Conceptual Mapping of Jungian Analytical Psychology onto Indian Knowledge Systems
items.subtitle: PSYARXIV · 精神分析 · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Manoj Kumar Mallick
items.summary: Carl Jung engaged Eastern thought throughout his career, writing psychological commentaries on The Secret of the Golden Flower, the Tibetan Book of the Dead, and Kuṇḍalinī yoga, yet this engagement remained impressionistic rather than systematic. No existing review pairs his core constructs with named terms from classical Indian philosophy. This paper proposes a term-by-term conceptual correspondence between six constructs of Jungian analytical psychology and six terms drawn from Sāṃkhya, Patañjali's Yoga, and Advaita Vedānta. It does not introduce a new theoretical model, acronym, or unifying framework. The paper follows Jaakkola's Theory Synthesis template for conceptual articles, distinguished from Theory Adaptation, Typology, and Model approaches. Four criteria guided term selection: definitional precision, scope-matching, textual traceability, and precision over popularity. Each correspondence was checked against primary Jungian texts and established secondary scholarship in Indology. Six correspondences are proposed: Collective Unconscious–Mahat, Archetypes–Tattva, Persona–Vyavahārika, Anima/Animus–Puruṣa/ Prakṛti, Shadow–Kleśa, and Individuation–Svarūpa-bodha. A central divergence emerged alongside these resemblances. Jung's individuation preserves a differentiated, related self, while Advaita's deeper vocabulary points toward non-dual dissolution of that self. This paper treats the divergence as a substantive finding, not a flaw in the method. The mapping offers culturally grounded vocabulary for teaching analytical psychology in Indian settings and for developing culturally resonant counseling language, illustrated through a brief clinical vignette. Risks of essentialism, translation distance, and untested clinical application are named explicitly, with concrete directions proposed for future empirical and textual work.

items.author: Myron Tsikandilakis, Persefoni Bali, Roland Erich Uriko, Mohammad Eskandari, Victoria-Maria Pasachidou, Romina Toranzos, Konrad Szczesniak, Ivona Dömischová, Pierre-Alexis Mével, Christopher R Madan, Alison Milbank
items.summary: The notion of subliminal processing often refers to perception that takes place below the threshold of conscious visual awareness. This is suggested to lead to behavioural and emotional changes with spontaneous and actionable evolutionary-survival and/or social-adaptation response value. Therefore, it has been suggested that the presentation of imperceptible visual elicitors can lead to responses, such as skin-conductance and heart-rate, and facial-emotional, and participant behavioural and self-report changes without conscious awareness. In a series of experiments, we disproved this theory. We showed that individually-adjusted, truly imperceptible elicitors did not induce any of these changes, when using null-hypothesis-testing, and, furthermore, provided evidence for null responses, when using Bayesian analyses. We proceeded to a series of novel and exploratory experiments on unconscious theory. We tested whether behavioural and emotional responses were reported to precede conscious awareness using overt presentations of visual-emotional elicitors. We showed evidence that the experience of physiological-emotional responses was reported to precede conscious awareness of a perceived visual-emotional content. These early responses were automatic and involuntary; they did not involve or require conscious access, or accessibility, and deliberation, and could not be physiologically restrained by conscious instruction for inhibition. We proposed that responses that can be termed unconscious, but not subliminal, are preceding, spontaneous and conditionally uninhibited experiential components of exposure to perceived, but not imperceptible, emotional elicitors. We extended that they involve genuine evolutionary-survival and social-adaptation value, compared to so-called subliminal processes, because they enable spontaneously-occurring, and progressively-intentional and intended behavioural and emotional adjustments, and readjustments, and adapting refinements.

items.title: No evidence of unconscious learning in eye-tracking measures of contextual cueing
items.subtitle: PSYARXIV · 精神分析 · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Miguel A. Vadillo, Laura Cepero Amores, Han Bao, David Shanks
items.summary: We revisit the longstanding claim that movements of the eyes convey information that the viewer is unaware of. In the contextual cueing task, observers search for a target amongst distractors. Some distractor configurations repeat multiple times, and observers learn to locate the target in these configurations more and more rapidly – a selection history effect. Eye movements monitored in contextual cueing experiments can be analyzed in a wide range of different ways, including number of fixations before target identification, scanpath length, decision time after fixating the target, fixation duration and others. We conducted a meta-analysis on a range of such measures to estimate the contextual cueing effect size for each measure in 31 published studies. We then report an experiment in which the amount of information conveyed in seven eye-movement measures identified in the meta-analysis was compared to the amount available for conscious report and in response times. All measures showed contextual cueing effects. Employing an analytical approach which places direct (awareness) and indirect (eye-tracking) measures on a common scale, the results show that the amount of information conveyed in eye-movement measures never exceeds the amount available to awareness.

items.title: No need to invoke ‘unconscious attention’ to explain the perceptual advantage of targets presented to the same eye as a preceding cue
items.subtitle: PSYARXIV · 精神分析 · PREPRINT SIGNAL
items.author: Surya Gayet
items.summary: Claims about unconscious processing can profoundly impact theories of awareness, but require careful exclusion of simpler low-level explanations. Fuentes and Valle-Inclán (2026) report faster detection of targets presented to the same eye as a preceding monocular cue and interpret this effect as evidence that unconscious eye-of-origin information guides reflexive attention. Here, I argue that this conclusion is not warranted. Cue validity is fully confounded with transient shifts in ocular dominance caused by the presentation of the cue (i.e., flash suppression; Wolfe, 1984). The temporal dynamics of the reported validity effect are consistent with such an ocular-dominance account. Moreover, the assessment that eye-of-origin information was indeed inaccessible to consciousness does not meet current standards for establishing unconscious processing. Considering the existence of a more parsimonious interpretation of the data, based on well-established low-level visual phenomena, this set of experiments cannot be taken as evidence for unconscious guidance of reflexive attention.

(2006) with continuous flash suppression (Chen et al., 2026a) and gaze-contingent crowding (Chen et al., 2026b), we found evidence for attraction towards suppressed opposite-sex nude images in heterosexual individuals below the subjective, instead of the objective threshold of consciousness, as claimed by Jiang et al. items.title: Luria’s Studies on Speech and Neuroscientific Evidence: Limbic System Functions as Biological Foundations for Socio-Cultural Psychology and Psychoanalysis
